title: Excess one-hour pairs per M2+ event rose at The Geysers between 2004-2013 and 2014-2025
abstract: We tested short earthquake pairs across a previously reported Geysers rate change. A fixed ComCat snapshot has 3,385 M2+ events in 2004-2013 and 2,398 in 2014-2025. We counted unordered pairs within one hour in each UTC month. We subtracted the expected count for independent uniform times with the same monthly totals. Excess pairs per event rose from 0.1026 to 0.1922. The later-minus-earlier change was 0.0896, with a conditional 95% year-bootstrap interval of 0.0360 to 0.1486. Two-year blocks and fixed daily counts also gave positive intervals. The M2.5+ check was uncertain. Excess pairs per year had no clear change: the later/earlier ratio was 1.106, with an interval of 0.759 to 1.635. Thus, more excess pairs per event does not establish more bursts per year. The result does not measure a triggered-event fraction or identify a physical cause. Same-source boundary selection, detection changes, mixed magnitudes, time dependence and a uniform-time reference limit inference. The package contains original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and a scalar audit. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Excess pairs per event and later-minus-earlier contrasts. Lines show conditional 95% bootstrap intervals. The daily check changes the reference; other checks change the sample or gap.

citations.reason: The reported unexplained rate drop sets the period boundary. We test short pairs, not operation models. Same-source follow-up, not independent confirmation.
Prior magnitude-fraction test in the same snapshot. Its M2.5 sensitivity and scale limits inform interpretation.
Shared source snapshot and prior weekly-phase null; we use a different statistic and new code.
